context.problem: Halyard's parts catalogue search misses fitment matches, so counter staff fall back to paper microfiche and customers get sent the wrong impeller.

goals.goal: Counter staff find the right part first time
goals.metric: wrong-part returns down 50% in two quarters

successMetrics: wrong-part returns halved within two quarters

actors.name: Counter salesperson
actors.goal: find a part by engine model, not part number
painPoints: search only matches exact part codes

actors.name: Trade customer
actors.goal: check a part fits their engine before ordering
painPoints: no fitment data on the public site

workflows.name: Parts lookup
workflows.trigger: customer describes their engine at the counter
exceptions: superseded part numbers are not linked to their replacement

requirements.text: Search must match parts by engine make, model and year, not only by part number.
requirements.label: confirmed

requirements.text: Search results must show whether a part is superseded and link to its replacement.
requirements.label: confirmed

requirements.text: The fitment index must rebuild nightly from the supplier catalogue feed.
requirements.label: assumed
requirements.source: inferred from the weekly supplier feed mentioned in the call

requirements.text: Counter staff should be able to filter results by depot stock.
requirements.label: recommended
requirements.source: analyst recommendation — most call-backs are stock questions

businessRules.rule: A superseded part number always resolves to its newest live replacement, following the chain to the end.

scenarios.when: staff search by make, model and year
scenarios.then: fitting impellers are listed with fitment confidence

nfrs.text: Search must return within 400ms at the counter on 180,000 catalogue rows.
nfrs.label: confirmed

constraints.text: Work lands in the existing halyard-catalog repository — Next.js frontend, Postgres, no rewrite.
No new infrastructure: search stays on the existing Postgres instance.

assumptions.text: The supplier feed carries fitment data for at least the top 20 engine makes.

openQuestions.question: How deep do supersession chains go in the current data?
openQuestions.reason: changes whether resolution is recursive or single-hop
